premise: I used $143,000 of my late husband’s life insurance after 27 years as a mail carrier to buy a century-old six-unit apartment house with my son-in-law, who signed a 45% stake and a lifetime lease for the ground-floor unit; when a developer offered $910,000 for the property, he forged a deed transfer, sold the building, and left me a $5,200 'vacancy' check. I recovered the original co-ownership agreement from a fireproof lockbox hidden in the basement laundry room, voided the sale, and now run 'Unit of Deceit Rentals,' where he unclogs drains in a coverall that says 'Drained My Trust' and every lease prints his deed-fraud docket.
